title: Hiware Bazar's turnaround
body: Hiware Bazar is a village in Ahmednagar district of Maharashtra. For years it suffered from frequent droughts, and its farmers got poor yields from their fields. Popatrao Baguji Pawar was then elected its Sarpanch. Following Anna Hazare's model, he began rainwater harvesting and watershed conservation, and lakhs of trees were planted. These steps helped to recharge the groundwater. The villagers worked together with their Sarpanch on these efforts, and within a few years Hiware Bazar became green and prosperous. In 2020, Popatrao Pawar was awarded the Padma Shri.

title: The Children's Parliament of rural Rajasthan
body: A few decades ago, Bunker Roy's Barefoot College initiative gave rise to a 'Children's Parliament' in rural Rajasthan. Underprivileged children aged 8 to 14 attended night schools and took part in parliament-like elections. The process followed formal steps: children had voter ID cards and candidates campaigned for votes. The elected representatives formed a 'Cabinet' that looked after the management of schools and spoke up for the needs of the community. Children raised issues such as access to education, sanitation and social equality. The initiative built leadership and social awareness, and it received many honours, including the World's Children's Honorary Award in 2001.
